newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close lackluster day mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close lackluster day mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed a lackluster session mixed, with key contracts barely budging from tight intraday ranges.
Comments from various European officials regarding European Monetary Union failed to exert any upside or downside pressure on mark or Swiss franc futures prices.
"We had a steady stream of comments yesterday, and the market gets a little immune to them," said Earl Johnson, foreign exchange economist at the Bank of Montreal in Chicago.
However, underlying speculation that the start date for the EMU will be delayed continued to support marks, he said.
While mark futures were lower, June bounced off Tuesday's low of $0.5968 and held above support at $0.5962, which corresponds to dollar/mark resistance at 1.6870, traders said.

Since 1100 CST/1700 GMT, June marks traded between $0.5973 and $0.5989, unfazed by a series of EMU comments by European officials, from Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg to British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind.

While Rifkind said a single European currency would divide the European Union for a generation to come, Duisenberg, who becomes chief of the European Monetary Institute this summer, supported a strict reading of the Maastricht treaty.
Another EU official said he had no doubt the EMU would start on time and with no softening of the criteria.
Traders said the market was beginning to shift its focus to Germany's economic growth rate, particularly after western Germany's February Ifo business climate index rose slightly.
"There is a sense of, 'How much worse can things get in Germany and how much better can things get in the U.S.?'," one currency futures broker said.
Johnson said signs of economic growth in Germany, coupled with no U.S. rate hike by the Federal Reserve next week, could raise beliefs that the dollar has set a near-term top.
"You are already hearing about some looking for the dollar to test 1.62 before rising to 1.80," he said. Those spot levels correspond to $0.6208 and $0.5590 in June marks.
The 0.3 percent rise in the overall U.S. February Consumer Price Index reported Wednesday morning failed to raise expectations for a rate hike next week, traders and analysts said.
"I'm not convinced that they are ready to launch a pre-emptive strike," Johnson said.
However, concerns about higher U.S. rates pushed June Canadian dollar futures lower, traders said.
June Canadian dollars fell through key support at $0.7300, paving the way for further losses, they said.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was off $0.000024 at $0.008243, marks were down $0.0029 at $0.5982, Swiss francs were $0.0022 lower at $0.6992, sterling rose $0.0102 at $1.5970, Canadian dollars were down $0.0018 at $0.7306, Australian dollars were $0.0016 lower at $0.7864 and Mexican pesos were $0.000075 higher at $0.121125.
